scenarios.name: Global Supply Chain Stabilization
scenarios.description: Resolution of major supply chain bottlenecks due to improved logistics and diplomatic agreements, reducing inflationary pressures.

impacts.explanation: Reduced supply chain costs lower production expenses and consumer prices.
Stabilized supply chains may reduce government stimulus needs.

scenarios.reasoning: Based on historical patterns of supply chain stabilization post-crisis, combined with ongoing diplomatic efforts in key trade regions.
tetlockCommandments: Break seemingly intractable problems into tractable sub-problems

scenarios.name: Escalating U.S.-China Trade War
scenarios.description: Increased tariffs and sanctions escalate tensions, disrupting global trade flows and technology dependence.

impacts.explanation: Worsening trade deficit from reduced exports and increased imports.
Higher yields due to investor flight to safety and increased government borrowing costs.

scenarios.reasoning: Recent geopolitical rhetoric and historical precedent of U.S.-China tensions suggest moderate likelihood of escalation.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between inside and outside views

scenarios.name: Central Bank Policy Tightening
scenarios.description: Federal Reserve raises rates further to combat embedded inflation, increasing borrowing costs.

impacts.explanation: Direct policy action increases short-term interest rates.
Higher borrowing costs reduce business investment and hiring.

scenarios.reasoning: Persistent inflation metrics and inflation-targeting mandates make rate hikes probable if CPI remains elevated.
tetlockCommandments: Strive to distinguish as many degrees of doubt as the problem permits

scenarios.name: Energy Price Collapse
scenarios.description: Sudden drop in oil prices due to OPEC+ output increases or recessionary demand decline.

impacts.explanation: Lower energy costs reduce input prices for transportation and manufacturing.
Cheaper energy stimulates consumption and production.

scenarios.reasoning: Current energy reserves and economic slowdown signs in major markets could trigger price corrections.
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem

scenarios.name: Housing Market Correction
scenarios.description: Sharp decline in housing starts and prices due to interest rate sensitivity and reduced buyer sentiment.

impacts.explanation: Direct impact from sustained high mortgage rates.

scenarios.reasoning: Recent housing starts decline (-15.45%) suggests fragility in the sector against monetary policy shifts.
tetlockCommandments: Balance under- and overreacting to evidence

scenarios.name: Global Pandemic Resurgence
scenarios.description: New health crises in major trading partners disrupt labor and supply chains.

impacts.explanation: Labor shortages and business closures increase joblessness.
Consumer spending declines due to health fears and disrupted travel.

scenarios.reasoning: Pandemic risk scenarios remain in Tetlock models due to historical precedent and global health vulnerabilities.
tetlockCommandments: Master the error-balancing cycle: Try, fail, analyze, adjust, try again

methodology: Applied Tetlock's pillars through probabilistic scenarios weighted by geopolitical and economic factors, balancing inside/outside views and updating forecasts iteratively.
geopoliticalSummary: Moderate risk of China-U.S. trade tensions, potential for conflict in Eastern Europe, and ongoing global health vulnerabilities.
geoeconomicSummary: Supply chain stability remains uncertain, energy prices show volatility, and digital economy growth contrasts with traditional manufacturing weakness.
currentEventsSummary: Recent Fed policy signals, persistent trade deficits, and housing market slowdown observed in latest economic reports.
